top_10.title: First time contributing? Start here.
top_10.body:
Welcome 👋

If you've never contributed to AiSOC before, here's the shortest path from "interesting repo" to "merged PR".

## Step 1 — See AiSOC actually running

```bash
git clone https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC && cd AiSOC
make up      # the CORE profile — the real pipeline
make smoke   # prove it: one real event in, a retrievable alert out
```

`make up` creates `.env`, generates every secret in it, creates an administrator and **prints its password once** — copy it. Then sign in at <http://localhost:3000> (API docs at <http://localhost:8000/api/docs>). `make smoke` reports PASS or FAIL for each stage, so you know the pipeline works rather than assuming it:

```
[PASS] raw telemetry accepted by ingest
[PASS] event traversed the spine and became an alert
[PASS] alert is retrievable by id from the API
```

Needs Docker Compose v2 with 8 GB memory and 20 GB free disk in the Docker VM, plus `python3` and `bash`. `make doctor` checks all of it and diagnoses a stack that won't come up. [Installation](https://beenuar.github.io/AiSOC/docs/installation) says what each number was measured against.

**Zero install:** [open in GitHub Codespaces](https://codespaces.new/beenuar/AiSOC?quickstart=1) and run the same commands, then click the forwarded port 3000 in the **Ports** panel.

Once it's up, `make demo` loads labelled synthetic data on top — including `/cases/INC-RT-001?tab=ledger`, a LockBit 3.0 ransomware case the agent has investigated. Click through the **Investigation Ledger** so you've seen what AiSOC does. Every seeded row carries `is_synthetic=true` and the console labels it as such.

> One thing to avoid: `pnpm aisoc:demo` brings up `infra/compose/docker-compose.demo.yml`, which is a **UI preview only** — no ingest service, no fusion service, and Kafka disabled. The file says so in its own header. It's fine for looking at the interface, but it can't tell you whether AiSOC works. Use `make up` for that.

## Step 2 — Pick a small, scoped task

The [`good first issue`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/issues?q=is%3Aopen+label%3A%22good+first+issue%22) list is the first place to look — comment on one saying you'd like to take it. It's often thin, so these standing tasks are always open:

- **Add a detection.** New rules go under [`detections/`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/tree/main/detections) with positive *and* negative fixtures in [`detections/fixtures/`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/tree/main/detections/fixtures). Read [`detections/README.md`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/detections/README.md) first — it explains the four tiers and what "executable" means here (a rule replayed through the real engine and watched to fire, which is not the same as a rule that detects an attack).
- **Add a connector.** One Python class per source under [`services/connectors/app/connectors/`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/tree/main/services/connectors/app/connectors). [Hello, connector](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/apps/docs/docs/connectors/hello-connector.md) is an end-to-end tutorial that builds a real one against a free no-auth API, so you can follow it without a vendor account. Requests and votes live in the [connector wishlist (#356)](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/issues/356).
- **Write a hunt.** Hunt-as-Code YAML hypotheses under [`hunts/`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/tree/main/hunts); [Hello, hunt](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/apps/docs/docs/detections/hello-hunt.md) walks through one.
- **Add a playbook** under [`playbooks/`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/tree/main/playbooks).
- **Fix a typo or improve a doc page** under [`apps/docs/docs/`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/tree/main/apps/docs/docs).

## Step 3 — Make the change, open a PR

Commits need a sign-off (`git commit -s`); `git commit --amend -s --no-edit` fixes the last one and `git rebase --signoff main` fixes a branch.

The default [pull-request template](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/.github/pull_request_template.md) walks you through what we need. The eval-harness section is required for substrate, playbook and detection changes — tick "Not applicable" otherwise.

Two things worth knowing before your first PR, because they're enforced and they surprise people:

- **Every published claim has to be true.** If you add a link it must resolve, and if you state a number it has to come from the tree rather than from memory. CI checks a lot of this.
- **No mock or fabricated data in the authenticated product.** Seeded and synthetic data is gated behind demo mode and labelled; honest empty and error states are the default everywhere else.

If you get stuck, [open a Q&A discussion](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/discussions/new?category=q-a) — don't suffer in silence.

The full contributor guide is [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md), and **Your first 30 minutes** near the top of it is a four-step version of this page.

Looking forward to your first PR. 🛡️

top_10.title: Connector wishlist — what should AiSOC ingest next?
top_10.body:
This is the rolling wishlist for **new connectors** the community would like to see ingested by AiSOC.

## How to vote / request

- 👍 the top comment for a connector you want.
- Reply with the *exact* product name + source format (REST? JSONL? syslog? S3 export?) + a link to the vendor's API docs. A signal score helps prioritisation: how many enterprises already rely on this in their SOC?
- If you've already shipped a custom connector for AiSOC, drop it here — even unmerged forks help.

## How to *build* one

**Start with [Hello, connector](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/apps/docs/docs/connectors/hello-connector.md)** ([on the docs site](https://beenuar.github.io/AiSOC/docs/connectors/hello-connector)). It is an end-to-end tutorial that builds a real, runnable connector against a free no-auth HTTP service, so you can walk every line of the contract — `schema()`, `test_connection()`, `fetch_alerts()`, `normalize()` and a smoke test — without a vendor account or an API key. [Connectors overview](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/apps/docs/docs/connectors/index.md) is the companion reference.

Connectors live under [`services/connectors/app/connectors/`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/tree/main/services/connectors/app/connectors), one Python class per source. The shape:

1. Subclass `BaseConnector` ([`base.py`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/services/connectors/app/connectors/base.py)) and declare a `schema()` returning a `ConnectorSchema` with the config fields your connector needs.
2. Pick a category. There are **nine**: `ai`, `cloud`, `edr`, `iam`, `ndr`, `network`, `saas`, `siem`, `vcs`.
3. Mark sensitive fields `secret=True` so the credential vault encrypts them at rest.
4. Register the class in `_CONNECTOR_CLASSES` **and `__all__`** in [`__init__.py`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/services/connectors/app/connectors/__init__.py). Discovery is registry-based, so there is no other wiring — but two artefacts are derived from that tuple and both are `--check`-gated in CI, so regenerate and commit them or the build reds:
   ```bash
   python3 scripts/generate_connector_count.py   # the "N connectors" claims
   python3 scripts/generate_connector_types.py   # the console's ConnectorType union
   ```
5. Add a marketplace manifest at `plugins/<connector-id>/plugin.yaml` mirroring `schema()`, then run `pnpm marketplace:sync`.
6. Preserve all five severity tiers in `normalize()` — `info | low | medium | high | critical`. If the vendor publishes a distinct `critical`, map it to `critical`; do not collapse it into `high`.
7. Nest the vendor payload under `raw_event` (not `raw`). The ingest normalizer's canonical-envelope check keys on that, and a connector that gets it wrong falls through to the generic profile, which is how events end up archived but never promoted to alerts.

Per-connector documentation pages under `apps/docs/docs/connectors/` are **generated** by [`scripts/generate_connector_docs.py`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/scripts/generate_connector_docs.py), which also owns the `Connectors` list in [`apps/docs/sidebars.ts`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/apps/docs/sidebars.ts) between its `GENERATED CONNECTOR LIST` markers — so run the generator rather than hand-editing the sidebar. A hand-written page wins over the generated one, but it still has to mention every required and secret field; the generator appends a marker-wrapped field reference to enforce that.

## Currently most-requested (auto-curated from comments)

_Maintainers will edit this list as votes pile up. PRs always welcome — the issue tracker is just the queue._

| Source | Category | Status |
|--------|----------|--------|
| _comments below feed this table_ |        |        |

## What already ships

**87 connectors** out of the box: 22 SaaS, 18 cloud, 17 SIEM, 10 EDR, 7 IAM, 7 network, 3 VCS, 2 NDR, 1 AI. The count is derived from the registry by `python3 scripts/generate_connector_count.py` and gated in CI, so check it there rather than trusting this paragraph.

The authoritative list is [`_CONNECTOR_CLASSES`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/services/connectors/app/connectors/__init__.py) or the [connectors overview](https://beenuar.github.io/AiSOC/docs/connectors). Not the marketplace — [`marketplace/index.json`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/marketplace/index.json) carries **77** plugin manifests against those 84 registered connectors, so it undercounts. (A missing manifest for your connector is itself a reasonable first PR.)

If your tool isn't in the catalog and you don't want to write code, **universal capture** may already cover it — webhook URLs, an email relay, CEF syslog and Splunk HEC let any vendor that can POST or send mail land events in the same OCSF stream.

top_10.title: [Feature]  Explicitly requested tasks
top_10.body:
## Problem / motivation

Explicitly requested tasks are currently handled through alert evaluation. A request can receive a “Created” response after being submitted for evaluation, without a persistent task being saved or appearing in “Needs you.”

This makes it difficult to determine whether a task exists, track its progress, or mark it completed. Acknowledging an alert also does not necessarily mean the underlying work is finished.

## Proposed solution

Add persistent user tasks with a lifecycle independent of alert evaluation.

Each task should have:

- A stable ID.
- Title and description.
- Owner.
- Status: open, in progress, waiting, or completed.
- Optional due date.
- Creation, modification, and completion timestamps.
- A reference to the originating conversation or message.

When a user explicitly requests a task, save it immediately and confirm creation only after storage succeeds. Alert evaluation may enrich or escalate the task, but should not determine whether it exists.

Allow users to view, update, complete, and reopen tasks through the UI and chat. Provide authenticated API endpoints for the same operations, with pagination, filtering, ownership checks, and conflict detection.

Completed tasks should be hidden from active views by default but remain accessible in history.

## Alternatives considered

- **Use alerts as tasks:** Alert acknowledgement and dismissal do not accurately represent task progress or completion.
- **Use activity logs:** Logs record submissions but do not provide a reliable task lifecycle.
- **Require tasks to pass alert evaluation:** Explicit user commitments should persist regardless of their urgency or relevance score.

## Scope

- [x] Backend (`packages/core`)
- [x] UI (`packages/ui`)
- [ ] A new specialist agent
- [ ] An integration (Slack / Email / Telegram / Discord / Google Chat)
- [ ] Deployment / infrastructure
- [x] Docs

## Additional context

Tasks and alerts should have distinct purposes:

- **Task:** Work someone has committed to doing.
- **Alert:** Information selected for someone’s attention.

They may be linked, but acknowledging or dismissing an alert should not automatically complete its associated task.

### Acceptance criteria

- Explicitly requested tasks persist independently of alert evaluation.
- Creation is confirmed only after successful storage.
- Users can update status, complete tasks, and reopen them.
- UI, chat, and API reflect the same saved task state.
- Completed tasks are excluded from active views by default.
- Repeated requests or retries do not create unintended duplicates.
- Failed operations report an error without claiming success.

top_10.title: Issues with scrollbar use in `Page` template main area
top_10.body:
#### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
In classic templates (Vanilla, Bootstrap, Fast, Material...), the scroll bar allowing to navigate within the main area was all the way to the right of the window which meant the cursor could be anywhere in the main area and it worked, even outside the actual main area container.

With `pn.ui.Page`, the scroll bar is within the main area container itself, with no margin, which proves frustrating to users.

First because on the web, to scroll through the main content of a page, you don't usually have to worry much about the position of your cursor. Plus, here it can become really bad if the main area is filled with elements that themselves can capture scroll events, such as plots, then the actual area where the scroll will reliably work can become vanishingly small. It's essentially only two tiny vertical bands on both sides of the plots.

Second, if you're looking for the scroll bar to actuate it by clicking on it, it's natural to look for it at the edge of the window.

#### Describe the solution you'd like
The idea would be to make `pn.ui.Page` behave like classic templates in that regard.

#### Describe alternatives you've considered
I think one could set a larger main area width and then place the actual content between two spacers. But still you may not necessarily end up with the scroll bar at the edge of the window.

Attached is an example showing how hard it becomes to scroll within a main area filled with holoviews plots. Unfortunately the cursor is not visible but you get the idea.

```python
import holoviews as hv
import numpy as np
import panel as pn

pn.extension()

plots = pn.ui.Column(
    *[
        hv.Curve(np.random.randn(100)).opts(height=400, responsive="width")
        for _ in range(5)
    ],
    width=800,
)

page1 = pn.ui.Page(
    main=[plots],
    sidebar_width=250,
    sidebar=["## I'm the sidebar"],
    main_width=800,
    title="I'm a title",
)
page2 = pn.template.MaterialTemplate(
    main=[plots],
    sidebar_width=250,
    sidebar=["## I'm the sidebar"],
    title="I'm a title",
)

page1.servable()
# page2.servable()  # For comparison purposes
```

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0c425bb6-bea9-4fd9-add7-e6d0077efe4b

- **Task:** Work someone has committed to doing.
- **Alert:** Information selected for someone’s attention.

They may be linked, but acknowledging or dismissing an alert should not automatically complete its associated task.

### Acceptance criteria

- Explicitly requested tasks persist independently of alert evaluation.
- Creation is confirmed only after successful storage.
- Users can update status, complete tasks, and reopen them.
- UI, chat, and API reflect the same saved task state.
- Completed tasks are excluded from active views by default.
- Repeated requests or retries do not create unintended duplicates.
- Failed operations report an error without claiming success.

issues.title: Issues with scrollbar use in `Page` template main area
issues.body:
#### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
In classic templates (Vanilla, Bootstrap, Fast, Material...), the scroll bar allowing to navigate within the main area was all the way to the right of the window which meant the cursor could be anywhere in the main area and it worked, even outside the actual main area container.

With `pn.ui.Page`, the scroll bar is within the main area container itself, with no margin, which proves frustrating to users.

First because on the web, to scroll through the main content of a page, you don't usually have to worry much about the position of your cursor. Plus, here it can become really bad if the main area is filled with elements that themselves can capture scroll events, such as plots, then the actual area where the scroll will reliably work can become vanishingly small. It's essentially only two tiny vertical bands on both sides of the plots.

Second, if you're looking for the scroll bar to actuate it by clicking on it, it's natural to look for it at the edge of the window.

#### Describe the solution you'd like
The idea would be to make `pn.ui.Page` behave like classic templates in that regard.

#### Describe alternatives you've considered
I think one could set a larger main area width and then place the actual content between two spacers. But still you may not necessarily end up with the scroll bar at the edge of the window.

Attached is an example showing how hard it becomes to scroll within a main area filled with holoviews plots. Unfortunately the cursor is not visible but you get the idea.

```python

import numpy as np

pn.extension()

plots = pn.ui.Column(
```

Flow scheduler stops firing jobs after some hours (eventlet worker); next_run_time stays in the past
issues.body:
Scheduled flows stop running without any error. The jobs stay in the jobstore, but their `next_run_time` stays in the past and nothing executes. Saving or re-activating a flow logs "Added job flow_workflow_N" with the new trigger time, but the job still doesn't fire. Manual runs keep working the whole time.

**Evidence** (checked on 2026-10-30 at about 09:02 IST)
Reading the jobstore table (`FLOW_JOBSTORE_TABLE`):

```
flow_workflow_23 2026-10-29 11:35:10   # interval flow, stuck since yesterday
flow_workflow_24 2026-10-29 11:36:02
flow_workflow_25 2026-10-29 11:36:02
flow_workflow_1  2026-10-30 08:55:00   # daily trigger, didn't fire at 08:55
```

At 08:54 the logs show `Creating daily trigger: 08:55` and `Added job flow_workflow_1`, but there's no log line at all at 08:55:00.

After `docker restart openalgo-web`, every job got a new future `next_run_time` and started firing again.

**Environment**

- Docker on ARM64 (Ubuntu).
- `gunicorn --worker-class eventlet --workers 1`.
- Container TZ, `tzlocal`, and the scheduler timezone are all `Asia/Kolkata`, so timezone isn't the cause.
- `BackgroundScheduler` with `SQLAlchemyJobStore` and `misfire_grace_time=60` (`services/flow_scheduler_service.py`).

**Suspected cause**
`BackgroundScheduler` runs in a thread under eventlet's monkey patching. The scheduler's wake-up thread seems to stall, so jobs are added but never woken. Possible fixes:

- Use `GeventScheduler` or an eventlet-friendly scheduler.
- Run the scheduler in a separate process.
- Add a watchdog that restarts the scheduler when a job's `next_run_time` falls behind.

Also, `misfire_grace_time=60` means a job that stalled is skipped instead of caught up. A missed scheduled run should at least be logged.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Activate flows with interval and daily schedule triggers.
2. Leave the container running for several hours. In my case it stalled about 1 hour after re-importing the flows on the previous day.
3. Check the jobstore `next_run_time` values. They're in the past and nothing runs until the container restarts.

issues.title: Agent message persistence commits SQLite synchronously on the controller loop
issues.body:
Part of the #2706 family (SQLite work on the controller loop). Found in the v3.2.1 post-tag upgrade run on a slow disk. Present since at least 3.2.0. Targets 3.2.2.

## Evidence

On the first Turn after the migration, the loop stalled for 3.0 s, 2.8 s and 3.9 s. The loop thread's stack, innermost frames last:

```
modules/agents/vibey/agent.py _settle → base.emit_result_message
core/controller.py emit_agent_message
core/message_dispatcher.py emit_agent_message → persist_agent_message
core/message_mirror.py persist_agent_message: with engine.begin() as conn
sqlalchemy ... do_commit → dbapi_connection.commit()
```

The wait is in the **commit** itself, not in acquiring SQLite's writer. On a slow disk, a commit's `fsync`, plus any WAL auto-checkpoint the commit triggers, runs synchronously on the loop thread. The test install's database was only 840 KB, which points at `fsync` latency rather than a large checkpoint.

## Why it is not a simple move to a thread (the #2708 check)

`persist_agent_message` runs for every persisted output: results, notices, interim rows, and hosted/tool-call trace rows. It runs on the loop today, so persists commit in the order the loop issued them. Two loop sections depend on that order:

1. **Within one emit.** The emit uses the persisted row (`persisted_output`): its id feeds delivery evidence and the Run's terminal record (`message_id`). Awaiting an off-loop persist in place keeps this order.
2. **Across concurrent emits for the same Session.** For example, a receiver's result and a concurrent Activity-output flush. The transaction assigns the row's position and transcript rank (`rank`, `message.new`, inbox). On the runtime-work executor, which has several threads, two persists could commit in the opposite order from the one the loop issued them in, and the transcript order would change.

The ordering requirement rules out the general door as is: transcript order must stay loop order.

## Proposed shape

Persist through an **ordered writer**: a single-thread executor that commits persists in the order the loop submitted them. Each emit awaits its own persist under the `_store_step` rule (#2715), so cancellation points stay where they are on master.

The post-commit publishes (`message.new`, `inbox.session.updated`, activity) go out from the loop after the commit lands, in the same order.

`persist_silent_terminal` and the other `message_mirror` writers go through the same writer.

## Placement

Right after path A (#2715), as A2: same emit path, same cancellation rule. Before B step 2. A short design check on the ordered writer comes first, covering:
- that cross-Session order needs no stronger guarantee than per-submission order;
- how the writer drains at shutdown;
- the plan-test-style regression: a held writer must not hold the loop, and two concurrent emits must keep their order.

issues.title: Document how to test agent skills and library changes through MCP in a live Revit
issues.body:
## Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe

Changing agent skills or the pyrevitlib helpers they describe is best verified by running the snippets in a live Revit through the MCP server. Nothing in the repo describes that workflow, so every contributor (human or agent) rediscovers it. `docs/agent-runtime.md` documents the in-Revit "Agent Tests" buttons and `AGENTS.md` documents the build and `pyrevit clones add` / `attach`. The steps in between are missing, and each one failed while I worked on #3839 (PR #3863):

- **A rebuild fails while any `pyrevit mcp` server is running.** Each MCP client session starts `bin\pyrevit.exe mcp`, which holds files in `bin\` (for example `Colorful.Console.dll`). `BuildLabsModule` then fails with "The process cannot access the file ... because it is being used by another process". The server of every open client session holds the lock, not only the current one.
- **Python and markdown changes under `pyrevitlib` need no rebuild.** IronPython can `reload()` them. CPython cannot: reloading `pyrevit.revit.db.create` fails with `TypeError: Duplicate type name within an assembly` because `FamilyLoaderOptionsHandler` is baked once. A restart of Revit is the reliable way to load edited modules on both engines.
- **The "Security - Unsigned Add-In" dialog appears after every rebuild and restart** and has to be accepted ("Load Once") before the MCP host answers. `docs/ci-cd.md` mentions this dialog only as a CI failure.
- **How to test a snippet or helper is undocumented:** run it through `run_query` in a scratch family or project document (`app.NewFamilyDocument`, `app.NewProjectDocument`), close the document in `finally`, and restore any user setting touched (for example `app.SharedParametersFilename`). If a script fails with a transaction open, `Close(False)` raises and hides the real error, so roll back first.

## Describe the solution you'd like

- A short section "Testing agent skills and library changes through MCP" in `docs/agent-runtime.md` that covers the steps above in order:
  - when a rebuild is needed (C# changes) and when a restart or reload is enough (Python and markdown)
  - stopping running `pyrevit mcp` processes before a rebuild, and that clients must reconnect afterwards
  - accepting the unsigned add-in dialog after each start
  - engine differences when reloading modules
  - running a snippet in a scratch document and cleaning up
- A one-line pointer to that section from `AGENTS.md`, which should stay a list of conventions and commands.
- Optionally, a small dev-tools command or script that stops the `pyrevit mcp` processes started from the clone's `bin\` before a build.

## Describe alternatives you've considered

- Put the whole procedure in `AGENTS.md`. It is loaded for every task and is meant to stay lean, so a pointer is enough.
- Leave it to the contributor. This is what happens now: one failed build and several extra runs before the cause of the lock was clear.
- Keep it in a personal notes file. That helps one person and not other contributors or their agents.

## Additional context

Found on Revit 2024.1, Windows 11, a Debug build of `develop`, IronPython 2.7.12 and CPython 3.12.3. Related: #3839, PR #3863.

issues.title: 413 请求体超限死锁：压缩请求也被挡，面板缺少上限开关
issues.body:
## 错误

图片型会话 token 压力 51%（509,860 / 1,000,000），请求体 16,967,637 bytes > 16,777,216，网关返回：

```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "payload too large (16967637 bytes > 16777216 limit)",
    "type": "invalid_request_error",
    "code": 413,
    "gateway_hint": "single request body exceeds the gateway cap (WB_MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES, default 16MB); raise it and restart wb-proxy"
  }
}
```

之后每轮都 413；`/compact` 发出的压缩请求也是普通 `/v1/messages` 请求，同样 413，死锁。

## 根因

- 413 在读 body 时就抛出（`_read_payload` 的大小检查 `wb_proxy.py:19689` → `_payload_or_error` `wb_proxy.py:19708`），发生在路由分发和任何压缩识别之前（调用点 `wb_proxy.py:22493`），压缩请求没有临时放宽。
- 413 文案是英文，只说 `raise it and restart wb-proxy`，没告诉用户可以发压缩请求或在面板调上限。
- `WB_MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES` 是启动环境变量（`wb_proxy.py:42`），面板没有开关。
- 字节 cap 不能改成 token：16MB 图片约 1 万 token，16MB 文本约 440-560 万 token。

## 修复建议

1. **413 改成中文、可行动**：

```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "请求体过大（16967637 字节 > 16777216 字节）",
    "type": "invalid_request_error",
    "code": 413,
    "gateway_hint": "请发送压缩请求（/compact）缩小上下文，或在网页面板「设置 → 单请求体上限」临时调高（当前 16MB）。"
  }
}
```

2. **面板增加「单请求体上限」MB 开关**：默认 16，范围 1-256，保存即生效（或提示重启）。

3. **压缩请求临时放宽到 64MB**：只对能识别的压缩请求生效；判定放在读 body 之前（header 此时已可读），给 `_read_payload` 传 64MB。普通请求仍 16MB。

issues.title: [yaxuanm/qdrant] Hybrid Search fails on named-vector collections (dense/sparse)
issues.body:
## Plugin
yaxuanm/qdrant v0.0.1

## Problem
Hybrid Search fails on collections with named vectors (`dense`, `sparse`) created outside the plugin (e.g. custom embed scripts).
**Error:** Qdrant responded with HTTP 400: Wrong input: Not existing vector name error:


## Root cause
1. Operation inference checks `text` before hybrid indicators → runs `operation: "query"` instead of `hybrid_search`
2. Plain query sends unnamed `vector` to `/points/search` — invalid when collection has only named vectors
3. Sparse vector is not generated from `text` in hybrid path (only dense embedding is created)
## Reproduction
- Collection: named vectors `dense` (3072) + `sparse`
- Tool: Qdrant · Hybrid Search
- Inputs: `text`, `using_dense: dense`, `using_sparse: sparse`, `fusion_method: rrf`
- Embedding: text-embedding-3-large
## Expected
`hybrid_search` → `/points/query` with prefetch using `dense` and `sparse`
## Actual
`query` → `/points/search` with flat `vector` array (no vector name)
## Fix verified locally (v0.0.2)
- Route hybrid before text→query
- Set `operation: hybrid_search` on hybrid tool YAML
- Generate sparse via `fastembed` (`Qdrant/bm25`)
- Add `fastembed` dependency
## Environment
- Dify 1.14.2 (self-hosted)
- Qdrant Cloud
- Plugin: yaxuanm/qdrant 0.0.1 from Marketplace

Social media management inside a Dify workflow: publish and schedule across twelve networks, read cross-account analytics, work a shared inbox, and build DM automations for Instagram, Messenger, WhatsApp and TikTok.

Scenarios people would build:

It returns a single-use approval URL that the account holder confirms inside Hive, and the call is re-sent with that token. Reads and draft creation run immediately. A plugin should surface the approval URL as output rather than treat it as an error.

issues.title: Stringsdict: all Russian plural entries are dropped on save, so the file is emptied and edits are never committed
issues.body:
### Describe the issue

On a **Stringsdict file** (`stringsdict`) component, saving the Russian translation writes an empty `<dict/>`. Every plural entry is dropped, including fully translated ones. The translations stay in the Weblate database, but they never reach the repository.

- File format: **Stringsdict file** (`stringsdict`), monolingual.
  - Base file: `<dir>/en.lproj/Localizable.stringsdict`
  - File mask: `<dir>/*.lproj/Localizable.stringsdict`
- All entries are simple single-variable plurals (`NSStringLocalizedFormatKey` = `%#@count@`, one `NSStringPluralRuleType` dictionary).
- Add-ons on the component: `weblate.autotranslate.autotranslate`. The component is linked to the main component (`weblate://<project>/<component>`).
- Languages: de, es, fr, it, ja, ko, pt_BR, ru, zh_Hans, zh_Hant. **Only `ru` is affected.** The others save and commit normally.

What we observe:

1. A Weblate commit replaced our Russian file, which had 21 translated entries, with an empty dict:
   ```xml
   <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
   <!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
   <plist version="1.0">
   <dict/>
   </plist>
   ```
   The commit message was "Translated using Weblate (Russian) – Currently translated at 100.0%".
2. Since then, **Download translation → original format** gives the empty file above, while **Download → CSV** contains all Russian plural translations (it is generated from the database).
3. Editing a Russian string in the UI and committing produces no commit and no push. The written file is the same empty dict every time, so git has nothing to commit and no pull request is updated.

#### Root cause

The bug is in translate-toolkit's `StringsDictFile.serialize()` (`translate/storage/stringsdict.py`). It was introduced in translate-toolkit **3.19.19** by commit `3367ed4a` ("fix(stringsdict): fold simple plural entries"), which fixed #21294:

```python
plural_tags = self._get_target_plural_tags(unit.target)
...
# Omit an untranslated or incomplete entry instead of writing
# a dictionary which Apple cannot resolve at runtime.
if (
    "other" not in plural_tags
    or not plural_strings[plural_tags.index("other")]
):
    continue
```

`plural_tags` comes from `translate.lang.data.plural_tags`. For `ru` (and also `pl`, `uk`, `be`) it is `["one", "few", "many"]`, and `_get_target_plural_tags()` adds `"zero"`, giving `['zero', 'one', 'few', 'many']`. **`"other"` is never in that list, so the condition is always true and every entry is skipped,** however complete the translation is.

The previous serializer wrote these entries correctly. Our Russian file round-tripped through Weblate for over a year before this change.

#### Proposed fix (translate-toolkit)

For languages without an `other` category, use the last category as the required fallback:

```diff
--- a/translate/storage/stringsdict.py
+++ b/translate/storage/stringsdict.py
@@ -288,11 +288,11 @@ class StringsDictFile(base.DictStore):
 
                 # Omit an untranslated or incomplete entry instead of writing
-                # a dictionary which Apple cannot resolve at runtime.
-                if (
-                    "other" not in plural_tags
-                    or not plural_strings[plural_tags.index("other")]
-                ):
+                # a dictionary which Apple cannot resolve at runtime. Languages
+                # such as Russian have no integer "other" category, their last
+                # category is the fallback instead.
+                fallback_tag = "other" if "other" in plural_tags else plural_tags[-1]
+                if not plural_strings[plural_tags.index(fallback_tag)]:
                     continue
```

Regression test, in the style of the existing `tests/translate/storage/test_stringsdict.py`:

```python
def test_single_plural_without_other_category(self) -> None:
    content = """<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0">
<dict>
    <key>items</key>
    <dict>
        <key>NSStringLocalizedFormatKey</key>
        <string>%#@count@</string>
        <key>count</key>
        <dict>
            <key>NSStringFormatSpecTypeKey</key>
            <string>NSStringPluralRuleType</string>
            <key>NSStringFormatValueTypeKey</key>
            <string>d</string>
            <key>one</key>
            <string>%d элемент</string>
            <key>few</key>
            <string>%d элемента</string>
            <key>many</key>
            <string>%d элементов</string>
        </dict>
    </dict>
</dict>
</plist>"""
    store = self.StoreClass()
    store.settargetlanguage("ru")
    store.parse(content.encode())

    assert store.units[0].target.strings == [
        "",
        "%d элемент",
        "%d элемента",
        "%d элементов",
    ]
    output = plistlib.loads(bytes(store))["items"]["count"]
    assert output["one"] == "%d элемент"
    assert output["many"] == "%d элементов"

    store.units[0].target = multistring(["", "%d элемент", "%d элемента", ""])
    assert plistlib.loads(bytes(store)) == {}
```

The last assertion keeps the intent of #21294: an entry whose fallback form is empty is still omitted.

An alternative would be to also emit an `other` key for these languages (CLDR uses `other` for fractional values in ru/pl/uk/be). That would change the number of plural forms shown in Weblate, so the change above is the minimal one.

#### Verified vs not verified

- Verified:
  - With translate-toolkit 3.20.1 (pinned by Weblate 2026.10.1), saving a translated Russian unit writes an empty dict.
  - The new test fails on unpatched code (`KeyError: 'items'`) and passes with the patch. The whole `test_stringsdict.py` suite passes (44 tests).
  - With the patched file installed in a `weblate==2026.10.1` environment, `StringsdictFormat` with our real `en` template and the empty `ru` file writes the Russian entry with its `one`, `few` and `many` forms.
  - translate-toolkit `main` at `888e46cc` (2026-10-29) still has the same check.
- Not verified:
  - Polish, Ukrainian and Belarusian; they are inferred from `translate.lang.data.plural_tags`.
  - The full Weblate test suite with the patch.
  - Apple runtime behaviour with a Russian dict without `other`. It worked in our app before 3.19.19.

### I already tried

- [x] I've read and searched [the documentation](https://docs.weblate.org/).
- [x] I've searched for similar filed issues in this repository.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

**In the UI**

1. Create a monolingual **Stringsdict file** component with base `en.lproj/Localizable.stringsdict` and file mask `*.lproj/Localizable.stringsdict`.
2. Add a Russian translation `ru.lproj/Localizable.stringsdict` with a complete simple plural entry (`one`/`few`/`many`). The **Standalone** example below has one.
3. Edit any Russian string in the editor and save.
4. Manage → Repository maintenance → Commit, or Files → Download translation (original format).
5. The Russian file is now `<dict/>`, and all entries are gone. After that, further Russian edits never produce a commit.

**Standalone (translate-toolkit only, no Weblate server)**

```python
# uv run --no-project --python 3.12 --with "translate-toolkit==3.20.1" python repro.py
import plistlib
from translate.storage.stringsdict import StringsDictFile

content = """<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0"><dict>
  <key>items</key><dict>
    <key>NSStringLocalizedFormatKey</key><string>%#@count@</string>
    <key>count</key><dict>
      <key>NSStringFormatSpecTypeKey</key><string>NSStringPluralRuleType</string>
      <key>NSStringFormatValueTypeKey</key><string>d</string>
      <key>one</key><string>%d элемент</string>
      <key>few</key><string>%d элемента</string>
      <key>many</key><string>%d элементов</string>
    </dict>
  </dict>
</dict></plist>"""

store = StringsDictFile()
store.settargetlanguage("ru")
store.parse(content.encode())
print(store._get_target_plural_tags(store.units[0].target))  # ['zero', 'one', 'few', 'many']
print(plistlib.loads(bytes(store)))                          # {}  <- entry dropped
```

Changing `settargetlanguage("ru")` to `"de"` (with `one`/`other` keys) writes the entry correctly.

### Expected behavior

A complete Russian (or Polish, Ukrainian, Belarusian) plural entry is written to the file, as it was before translate-toolkit 3.19.19. Only an entry whose fallback form is empty should be omitted, which was the intent of #21294.

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Exception traceback

```pytb

```

### How do you run Weblate?

weblate.org service

### Weblate version

2026.10.1 (translate-toolkit 3.20.1)

### Weblate deploy checks

```shell

```

### Additional context

- Introduced by translate-toolkit commit `3367ed4a` "fix(stringsdict): fold simple plural entries", released in **3.19.19** (2026-09-01) and present in 3.20.0, 3.20.1 and `main`. It was a follow-up to #21294.
- The wrong language data is in `translate/lang/data.py` → `plural_tags["ru"] == ["one", "few", "many"]` (same for `pl`, `uk`, `be`). `DECIMAL_EXTRA_TAGS` in the same file lists `other` for these languages, but `_get_target_plural_tags()` doesn't use it.
- Impact: every Russian translation edit made in Weblate is silently kept out of the repository, and the first such commit wipes the existing Russian file. The only workaround is to maintain the Russian `.stringsdict` directly in the repository and avoid editing Russian in Weblate.
- Related: #21294.

issues.title: feat(schema): honor conditional input requirements from model schemas
issues.body:
`scenario-sdk` 2.3.0 documents a fourth rule for when a model input is required, beside `always`, `ifDefined` and `ifNotDefined`:

```json
"required": { "conditional": { "values": { "<other input>": ["<value>", ...] }, "operator": "and" | "or" } }
```

The input is required when the named inputs hold one of the listed values; `operator` combines several conditions.

`_parse_required` in `scenario/core/schema/params.py` reads only `always`, `ifDefined` and `ifNotDefined`, so an input with a `conditional` rule is treated as optional. A user who sets the triggering value and leaves the input empty gets no requirement in the form, and the request is left for the service to reject.

To do:

- Parse `required.conditional` into the parameter spec, defaulting `operator` to the documented behavior.
- Apply it wherever the other requirement rules are applied today: the parameter controls (`params_ui.py`), render lanes and commands, `schema/forms.py` and the MCP tool schema (`tools_scenario.py`).
- Add schema tests for single and combined conditions.

Found while reviewing #638 (SDK 2.3.0 adoption), which does not change schema parsing.

issues.title: Any plans for i18n? I added Korean support in my fork
issues.body:
I'm Korean, and using Open Executive in English was getting in the way for me, so I added i18n with Korean in my fork: https://github.com/y0ngha/OpenExecutive/tree/feat/korean-ui

How it works:

- One setting, OE_LANGUAGE (ENGLISH by default, or KOREAN), picks the language for the whole deployment at runtime. With it unset, the English UI is unchanged.
- Web UI: text is moved into per-area English/Korean dictionaries with a small t() helper, no new dependency. Pages render per request, so a prebuilt Docker image follows the setting.
- Model output: prompts stay in English. For Korean, one fixed system block is added after the cached blocks, so prompt caching still works. Words the code parses (YES/NO, JSON and so on) stay in English.
- API text and the user guide: fixed messages the API shows use a localized(english, korean) helper, and the guide has Korean copies with an English fallback.
- Playbook and knowledge content stays in English, since the models read it.

Do you have any plans to support i18n? If so, I'd be happy to open a PR, split into smaller pieces if that's easier to review.

issues.title: HLSL input imports `float3x3 m = 1.0;` as `mat3 m = 1.0;`, which every target rejects
/trading: comparison legend rows draw over the symbol's OHLC readout
issues.body:
## What happens

On `/trading`, add a comparison symbol and move the crosshair over the chart. The comparison's legend row is drawn in the chart's top-left corner, on top of the terminal's own OHLC readout next to the symbol name. The row shows the comparison symbol, its close and its change, and it updates with the crosshair. The two readouts overlap and neither can be read.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open `/trading` on any symbol.
2. Add a comparison symbol.
3. Hover over the chart.

## Expected

Comparison rows stack below the OHLC readout and the SELL/qty/BUY panel, the way indicator legend rows already do.

## Cause

- **The terminal keeps the corner clear.** `frontend/src/lib/trading/terminal.ts` creates the chart with `legendOffset: { top: 80 }`, so canvas legend rows start below the OHLC readout and the trade panel.
- **The chart offsets indicator rows only.** openalgo-charts applies `legendOffset` only to indicator rows. Rows a host adds keep their own `top`, by design ("Host-added legend rows are left alone: the host positions its own", `src/core/chart-legends.ts`).
- **The comparison row is a host row with no `top`.** `TerminalComparisons.addLegend` in `frontend/src/lib/trading/terminalComparisons.ts` creates each comparison's `PaneLegend` without one, so it takes the default 6 px and lands on the readout.

Seen on 2.0.2.9; the same code is on `main` (2.0.3.1). A fix follows in a PR.

issues.title: Strategy module: batch legs are capped at 50 lots, and no leg order is split at the freeze limit
issues.body:
## What happens

On `/strategy/new`, the **Lots** box of a batch leg will not go above 50. Typing a larger number silently turns it into 50, and nothing on the page says why. The server refuses anything above 50 too, so a strategy with, say, an 80-lot NIFTY leg cannot be built.

- UI: [`Wizard.tsx` L347-356](https://github.com/marketcalls/openalgo/blob/dd198ba99529fb13c20ef97fa1f58345fab170ea/frontend/src/pages/strategy/Wizard.tsx#L347-L356) clamps the value with `Math.min(maxBatchQuantityFor(...), ...)`.
- Server: `MAX_LOTS = 50` in [`blueprints/strategy_module.py` L282](https://github.com/marketcalls/openalgo/blob/dd198ba99529fb13c20ef97fa1f58345fab170ea/blueprints/strategy_module.py#L282), applied to derivative legs at [L642](https://github.com/marketcalls/openalgo/blob/dd198ba99529fb13c20ef97fa1f58345fab170ea/blueprints/strategy_module.py#L642).

## Why raising the cap alone would not fix it

Each leg's entry and each leg's exit is sent as **one order**:

- The engine builds and dispatches a single order per leg, for entry ([`engine.py` L783](https://github.com/marketcalls/openalgo/blob/dd198ba99529fb13c20ef97fa1f58345fab170ea/services/strategy_module/engine.py#L783)) and for exit ([L1392](https://github.com/marketcalls/openalgo/blob/dd198ba99529fb13c20ef97fa1f58345fab170ea/services/strategy_module/engine.py#L1392)).
- Signal mode does the same ([`signals.py` L842](https://github.com/marketcalls/openalgo/blob/dd198ba99529fb13c20ef97fa1f58345fab170ea/services/strategy_module/signals.py#L842)).
- Nothing in `services/strategy_module/` or `blueprints/strategy_module.py` reads the freeze table, and no broker plugin slices orders itself.

The index freeze limits in `data/qtyfreeze.csv` (#2218) work out to roughly 50 lots:

| Underlying | Freeze qty | Lot size | Freeze qty ÷ lot size |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| NIFTY | 3,510 | 65 | 54 |
| FINNIFTY | 3,240 | 60 | 54 |
| BANKNIFTY | 1,440 | 30 | 48 |
| MIDCPNIFTY | 5,760 | 120 | 48 |
| NIFTYNXT50 | 1,125 | 25 | 45 |

So with a higher cap and no splitting, the failure would only move from the form to the exchange.

## Related problems

1. **The clamp is silent.** The operator never learns there is a limit, or what it is.
2. **50 is already above the freeze for three indices.** A BANKNIFTY or MIDCPNIFTY leg of 49-50 lots, or a NIFTYNXT50 leg of 46-50 lots, passes validation and then goes to the exchange as one order above the freeze quantity.
3. **Signal legs allow up to 10,000 lots** (`MAX_SIGNAL_LOTS`, [L274](https://github.com/marketcalls/openalgo/blob/dd198ba99529fb13c20ef97fa1f58345fab170ea/blueprints/strategy_module.py#L274)) through the same single-order dispatch, so anything above the freeze fails there as well.

## Possible fix

- **Proper fix:** split a leg's entry and exit into freeze-sized child orders, then raise or drop `MAX_LOTS`. The freeze lookup (`get_freeze_qty_for_option`) and the slicing in `services/split_order_service.py` already exist; scalping exits use them. This does change the engine's one-order-per-leg model (order rows, acknowledgement, fill reconciliation, recovery), so it seems worth agreeing on the design before a PR.
- **Smaller step in the meantime:** cap each leg at `floor(freeze / lot size)` for its underlying when a freeze is known, and show the limit and the reason instead of clamping silently. That covers problems 1 and 2.

Seen on 2.0.2.9; the same code is on `main` (2.0.3.1, dd198ba9).

issues.title: WhatsApp: add an "observe" group mode that records all messages and lets the owner track questions
issues.body:
## What

Add an `observe` mode for WhatsApp groups, like the Slack channel's `observe` mode.

In this mode the agent stays silent in the group, but every message from every
member is recorded (not only messages from the owner and `allowed_wa_ids`).
The owner can then, from the self-chat or the dashboard:

- look back over recent group history ("what questions were asked this week?")
- have the agent find questions raised in the group and track their status
  (open / answered / follow-up needed)
- get a private notification (self-chat or dashboard) when a new question
  appears or an open one goes unanswered too long

The agent should never post in the group in this mode.

## Why

I use WhatsApp groups for customer technical support. I need to know which
questions were asked, who answered, and what is still open, without the bot
speaking in the group.

Today this is not possible:

- `group_gate.py`: messages from members not in `allowed_wa_ids` are dropped
  before reaching the agent.
- `transport.py`: `fetch_history` returns `[]`, and messages from before the
  connection are dropped, so there is no history to look back on.
- Turns triggered by other members run with no tools, so the agent cannot
  record a question or notify the owner privately.

Adding members to `allowed_wa_ids` is not a workaround: it lets them make the
agent reply in the group, which I do not want.

## Additional Context

- Platform: macOS, Kiro Crew desktop app
- Channel: WhatsApp (linked device via neonize), 3 groups configured
- Nice to have: a configurable history window, and a dashboard view of
  tracked questions per group.

issues.title: test_file_utils umask tests assert against a umask the code never reads (import-time _UMASK), so they only pass on a 0o022 host
issues.body:
## Summary

`test_atomic_write_text_new_file_uses_umask_default` and `test_atomic_write_bytes_new_file_uses_umask_default` set a umask at runtime and assert the resulting file mode. `file_utils` captures the umask **once at import**, so the `os.umask(0o022)` the tests call has no effect on the code under test. The assertion therefore only holds on a host whose ambient umask already happens to be `0o022`, and fails outright on any other.

Observed on a host with `umask 0007`:

```
tests/comfy_cli/test_file_utils.py:163: AssertionError
assert 432 == (438 & ~18)
#      ^ 0o660, i.e. 0o666 & ~0o007 (the AMBIENT umask)
#              ^ 0o644, i.e. 0o666 & ~0o022 (the umask the test set)
```

Both tests fail the same way; `test_atomic_write_bytes_…` at `:313`.

## Cause

`comfy_cli/file_utils.py:98-105`:

```python
# The process umask, captured once at import. os has no getter, so reading it
# ...
# overlapping probes can restore each other's zero and strand the umask at 0.
_UMASK = os.umask(0)
os.umask(_UMASK)
```

Capturing once is deliberate and the comment gives a good reason for it. The tests simply do not account for it: they manipulate the real process umask, which `_atomic_write` no longer consults.

So this is a **test** defect, not a product one. The product behaviour the tests mean to pin — "a new destination gets the umask-derived default, not `mkstemp`'s hardcoded 0600" — is correct and worth keeping pinned; the tests just pin it against the wrong knob.

## Suggested fix

Patch the captured value rather than the process umask, so the test controls what the code actually reads:

```python
def test_atomic_write_text_new_file_uses_umask_default(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(file_utils, "_UMASK", 0o022)
    target = tmp_path / "fresh.json"
    atomic_write_text(target, "data")
    assert stat.S_IMODE(os.stat(target).st_mode) == (0o666 & ~0o022)
```

That also removes the `os.umask` save/restore, which is process-global state the current tests mutate.

A second case worth adding while in there: assert the same for a non-`0o022` umask (`0o077`, so `0o600`), which would have caught this — a single hardcoded umask value cannot distinguish "the code honours the umask" from "the host umask matches the literal in the assertion".

## Context

Found while verifying that pre-existing failures were unrelated to a converter change. Two other environment-sensitive failures turned up in the same run and are worth separating:

- Five `tests/comfy_cli/command/test_code_search.py::TestCodeSearchCLI` cases fail when the suite runs from inside an AI coding tool, because `CLAUDECODE` / `AI_AGENT` in the environment flip `detect_caller()` and `code-search` then passes `agent_origin=True`. Fixed in #1072.
- `test_node_deps.py::test_non_pep440_installed_version_is_unknown_not_a_crash` reports `mismatch` where it expects `unknown`. Not agent-env related (it fails with those vars unset) and I have not diagnosed it; noting it so it is not assumed covered by the other two.

None of these fail in CI, which is why they have survived: CI's environment happens to satisfy every one of the assumptions.



### Task Decomposition

Not decomposed: this is a two-test change in one file (swap `os.umask(...)` for `monkeypatch.setattr(file_utils, "_UMASK", ...)`, plus one extra parametrised umask value). Stated explicitly per the issue-filing convention.

- **Working Directory:** `/home/administrator/workspace/DCSProject/src`

## Summary
When using Jupyter MCP Server tools (specifically `read_notebook`) with file paths containing 'workspace/' as a prefix, the `normalize_filepath()` function incorrectly converts the relative path to an absolute path, dropping the 'workspace/' portion of the path.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Start Jupyter Server from `/home/administrator/`
2. Create a file at `/home/administrator/workspace/DCSProject/src/development_part_3.ipynb`
3. Use the Jupyter MCP Server tool `read_notebook` with the path `'workspace/DCSProject/src/development_part_3.ipynb'`
4. Observe the error

## Expected Behavior
The tool should correctly resolve the path to `/home/administrator/workspace/DCSProject/src/development_part_3.ipynb` and read the file successfully.

## Actual Behavior
The tool fails with `FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '/home/administrator/development_part_3.ipynb'`

## Error Log
```
[10/17/26 16:20:40] Error calling tool 'read_notebook'                                                                  
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/home/administrator/workspace/environments/jupyter/lib/python3.14/site-packages/fastmcp/server/server.py:1359 in call_tool
  File "/home/administrator/workspace/environments/jupyter/lib/python3.14/site-packages/fastmcp/tools/base.py:421 in _run
    ... 4 frames hidden ...
  File "/home/administrator/workspace/environments/jupyter/lib/python3.14/site-packages/jupyter_ai_tools/toolkits/notebook.py:197 in read_notebook
   194 │   │   The notebook content as a markdown string.
   195 │   """
   196 │   try:
→ 197 │   │   notebook_dict = await read_notebook_json(file_path)
   198 │   │   notebook_md = notebook_json_to_md(notebook_dict, include_outputs=include_outputs)
   199 │   │   return notebook_md
   200 │   except Exception:
  File "/home/administrator/workspace/environments/jupyter/lib/python3.14/site-packages/jupyter_ai_tools/toolkits/notebook.py:242 in read_notebook_json
   239 │   │   return payload["content"]
   240 │
   241 │   normalized_path = normalize_filepath(file_path)
→ 242 │   with open(normalized_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
   243 │   │   notebook_dict = json.load(f)
   244 │   │   return notebook_dict
   245
FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory:
'/home/administrator/development_part_3.ipynb'
```

## Root Cause Analysis
The `normalize_filepath()` function in `jupyter_ai_tools/toolkits/notebook.py:242` appears to be incorrectly handling paths that contain 'workspace/'. When given a relative path `'workspace/DCSProject/src/development_part_3.ipynb'`, it incorrectly normalizes it to `'/home/administrator/development_part_3.ipynb'` instead of the correct `'/home/administrator/workspace/DCSProject/src/development_part_3.ipynb'`.

## Workaround
Currently, the only workaround is to:
1. Either use absolute paths (which may not be supported by all tools)
2. Or adjust the directory structure to avoid the 'workspace/' prefix

## Impact
This bug affects all Jupyter MCP Server tools that rely on file path resolution, particularly in environments where files are organized under directories named 'workspace/', which is a common pattern in development environments and containers.

## Additional Context
- This was discovered while trying to insert a cell into a notebook file using Jupyter MCP tools
- Other paths without the 'workspace/' prefix seem to work correctly
- The bug appears to be in the path normalization logic, not in the basic file reading functionality

issues.title: [BUG] Empty Claude reply fails the run on the direct Anthropic transport (400)
issues.body:
Found while testing LLM provider integrations in agent frameworks: an automated tool flags candidates and each one is reproduced before it is reported. Reproduced on 7e1e5fe (main) against a local fake endpoint, not the live API.

**Describe the bug**
With `PIPESHUB_AGENT_TRANSPORT=direct` and an Anthropic model, a turn where Claude sends back nothing fails the run with a 400 instead of recovering.

The empty reply is stored as an `AssistantMessage`, and `AnthropicTransport` replays it as `{"type": "text", "text": ""}`. Anthropic refuses that with `messages: text content blocks must be non-empty`. The recovery is what sends it: `completion_gate` adds the "Your last reply came through empty" nudge, and the request carrying the nudge also carries the empty block. A thinking-only reply cut off at `max_tokens` fails the same way through the continuation note.

The LangChain arm recovers from the same reply, because langchain-anthropic drops the empty turn.

**To Reproduce**
Real `Agent`, `completion_gate` and the transport `build_direct_transport` picks, with a local endpoint standing in for Anthropic. Its first reply is `{"content": [], "stop_reason": "end_turn"}`, and it answers an empty text block with the error above.

```python
llm = get_generator_model("anthropic", {"configuration": {"apiKey": key, "model": "claude-sonnet-5"},
                                        "isReasoning": True, "isDefault": True})
transport = build_direct_transport(llm, model_name="claude-sonnet-5")
# Agent(spec, runtime) with this transport, streaming on
agent.runtime.hooks.on(HookEvent.POST_MODEL).use(completion_gate(context))
result = await agent.run(Goal(description="What changed this week?"))
```

The second request has roles `user, assistant, user`, with this assistant message:

```text
{"role": "assistant", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": ""}]}
```

and the run ends with:

```text
success=False output=None
LLM call failed: Anthropic API error (stream): Error code: 400 - ... 'message': 'messages: text content blocks must be non-empty'
```

The history on its own shows it too: `transport.complete([UserMessage("..."), AssistantMessage(content=""), UserMessage("Please continue.")])`.

**Expected behavior**
The empty turn is left out of the request, the nudge goes out, and the run continues as it does on the LangChain arm.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Linux
 - Version/Commit ID: `2113fd2`
 - `PIPESHUB_AGENT_TRANSPORT=direct`, provider Anthropic, `claude-sonnet-5`

**Related issues**
None found. #4089 reworded the nudge and did not touch this.

**Additional context**
Cause: `_format_message` falls back to an empty text block when an assistant message has no text and no tool calls ([anthropic.py#L287](https://github.com/pipeshub-ai/pipeshub-ai/blob/2113fd22f94f4a5daa25a9e995ae279dc1d17532/backend/python/app/agent_loop_lib/transport/anthropic.py#L287)).

The 400 in the output comes from the local endpoint, which copies the real message. Real reports of that error on this shape: [block/sprout#559](https://github.com/block/sprout/pull/559) (empty `end_turn` reply, same fallback) and [anthropics/claude-code#88536](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/88536) (assistant `{"type":"text","text":""}` replayed to api.anthropic.com). Anthropic documents empty `end_turn` replies and says to "add a continuation prompt in a new user message rather than retrying with the empty response" ([stop reasons](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/handling-stop-reasons)).

Fix idea: skip such a turn in `AnthropicTransport._format_messages`, which leaves `_format_message` and the test pinning its fallback alone. Two user messages in a row are fine, the API merges them, and it is what the LangChain arm already sends.

```python
if isinstance(msg, AssistantMessage) and not msg.tool_calls and not msg.text.strip():
    continue
```

issues.title: [Plugin Request]: Baizhi Agent Toolkit - web search, scraping, and extraction
issues.body:
### Plugin Name

Baizhi Agent Toolkit

### Function Description

Hi Dify team,

I maintain Baizhi Cloud's Agent Toolkit integrations and coordinate product operations. I am submitting this request through `ct-jaryn` on behalf of Baizhi Cloud. We would like to contribute and maintain a native Tool Plugin, and would appreciate feedback on whether the following scope fits the Marketplace's expectations for a distinct integration.

Baizhi Agent Toolkit is a hosted commercial tool service, not an LLM inference provider. Users need their own Baizhi account and API key; tool calls can consume service credits. Our [official integration repository](https://github.com/chaitin/baizhi-agent-toolkit) publishes integration configuration, documentation, and tests, not the hosted backend implementation.

The proposed plugin itself would be free and open source; Baizhi's hosted service usage would be billed separately under its service terms.

#### Proposed user experience

Install the plugin, authorize it with a required provider-level `secret-input` and a link to the [Baizhi console](https://agent-toolkit.app.baizhi.cloud/), then select one of three typed tools in a Workflow or Agent:

- **Web search** (`websearch_search`): search public web sources with query, freshness, result-count, and source-filter parameters.
- **Read a web page** (`web_scrape`): retrieve a page's content from a user-supplied HTTP(S) URL.
- **Extract structured information** (`web_extract`): request specified fields or instruction-driven extraction from a page.

The plugin would use a fixed Streamable HTTP endpoint, `https://agent-toolkit.app.baizhi.cloud/mcp`, with `Authorization: Bearer <user-provided key>`. The credential would not be a model-supplied tool parameter. Public examples, source code, packages, and CI would contain no real key.

#### Difference from existing MCP support

Dify already supports remote MCP and custom headers, and the Marketplace already has general-purpose MCP clients. We are not requesting another generic MCP connector or claiming that native MCP support is missing.

The intended contribution is a service-specific provider credential flow and three stable, typed workflow tools, with maintained parameter/output mapping, bounded errors, documentation, and compatibility tests. The plugin would not accept arbitrary remote tool names or automatically expose newly discovered capabilities. Provider credential validation would use initialization and tool discovery only, not a billable tool invocation. This needs to earn its place as a focused integration rather than merely rebrand a generic client.

#### Safety and review scope

Although the plugin's own MCP connection has a fixed destination, page scraping and extraction delegate user-supplied URL retrieval to the hosted service. We would conservatively disclose **High risk** under the current arbitrary-URL-fetching/crawling criteria, document request timeouts and data flow, and not infer low risk from the fixed transport endpoint. No code execution, shell access, cloud sandbox, payment, or arbitrary-tool forwarding is proposed.

The plugin would need an accurate privacy policy covering the data sent to Baizhi and relevant downstream services, plus credential/logging safeguards. We will not invent data-retention, residency, or no-logging guarantees. The adapter's open-source license and the hosted service's account/usage terms would be disclosed separately.

#### Contribution status and next steps

We have completed a local three-tool prototype from a previously recorded, credential-free tool-schema snapshot. Its 55 offline tests pass with the actual Dify and MCP SDKs and in-memory HTTP transports; a separate local review and rerun also passed. The tests cover provider declarations, typed input mapping, discovery-only credential checks, the fixed endpoint, redirect rejection, bounded discovery, and credential/error/log redaction. These are local results; reviewable source and release artifacts have not yet been published.

The prototype has not been accepted into the Marketplace, validated in a real Dify Community Edition or Cloud workspace, or newly tested against the production service. Historical schemas may have changed. URL validation is not a complete server-side request-forgery defense, and a post-parse output-size check is not a strict transport-memory bound. This issue remains a plugin-scope request, **not a packaged submission or a completed compatibility claim**.

Before a release PR, we would publish reviewable plugin source and setup/troubleshooting documentation, verify current tool schemas and a limited live flow with a dedicated revocable key, complete Dify installation/credential/tool tests, confirm the privacy disclosure and Developer Agreement, and submit one validated `.difypkg` through this repository's current template. Agreement and unperformed-test checkboxes will not be pre-checked.

We would welcome guidance if an existing integration or a different contribution route is more appropriate. Thank you for considering the proposal; the Baizhi team would be glad to cooperate on a maintainable integration that fits Dify's architecture and review standards. This request does not imply Dify endorsement or an established partnership.

### Official Website URL

https://baizhi.cloud/landing/agent-toolkit

issues.title: [Plugin Request]: AnySearch — unified general + vertical AI search
issues.body:
### Plugin Name

AnySearch

### Function Description

**API Docs**

API base: `https://api.anysearch.com` · MCP: `https://api.anysearch.com/mcp`

**Function Description**

AnySearch is a unified search API built for AI agents: one endpoint serving both general web search and vertical, structured data retrieval. We would like to publish it as a community tool plugin in the `search` category (`tags: [search]`, same shape as the official Tavily / Brave providers), and we would rather confirm with the maintainers first that it is welcome alongside the existing search providers — and whether you would prefer a different tag, scope, or risk framing.

**Proposed plugin surface** — three tools, Python 3.12 runner, minimal dependency footprint (`requests` only):

| Tool | Endpoint | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `anysearch_search` | `POST /v1/search` | Unified search. `query` (required), `tag` (`{domain}.{sub_domain}`, e.g. `code.doc`), `params` (object, tag-specific, e.g. `{"ticker":"AAPL"}`), `zone` (`cn` / `intl`), `language`, `max_results` (1–10), `format` (`json` / `markdown`) |
| `anysearch_capabilities` | `GET /v1/sub-domains` | Returns available domains, capability tags and their parameter definitions. Does **not** consume search quota. |
| `anysearch_extract` | `POST /v1/extract` | Fetch and extract clean content (HTML / plain text / JSON / Markdown) from a public URL |

The provider credential would be a `secret-input` API key that is **optional**: unauthenticated calls work against a per-IP rate-limited daily free tier, so users — and reviewers — can evaluate the plugin before signing up. Authenticated calls use `Authorization: Bearer <key>` against a paid quota.

**Why this is not a duplicate of the existing search providers**

The official providers are either general web search (Google, Bing, Brave, DuckDuckGo, Tavily, Serper, SearchApi, SearXNG, Perplexity) or extract/crawl (Jina, Firecrawl). The community vertical ones are single-purpose and region-bound (Google Scholar, Bilibili Search, Webz News Search, Bocha, Baidu AI Search, ZhipuAI Web Search). AnySearch differs on these specific points:

1. **General and vertical from the same endpoint and the same key.** A plain call behaves like general web search; adding `tag=finance.quote` with `params={"type":"crypto"}` returns live market quotes instead of blue links. No second vendor, no second credential, no second plugin.
2. **The vertical catalog is data, not a build-time schema.** `GET /v1/sub-domains` returns the available domains, tags and parameter definitions (`description`, `required`, `sort_order`) at runtime, at no quota cost. The plugin surface therefore stays at three tools as the catalog grows, instead of needing a new tool or plugin release per vertical.
3. **Intent routing and result fusion.** Per our docs, `/v1/search` routes the query to the best underlying sources by intent and then fuses and re-ranks the results — the caller does not pick an engine or merge result sets by hand.
4. **Region routing.** `zone: cn | intl` selects the result universe inside one API, instead of needing separate CN and global plugins.
5. **No-key first run.** Verified: an anonymous `POST /v1/search` returns `code: 0` with results, so a user can try the tool before creating an account.
6. **Low integration cost.** An MCP server is already live over Streamable HTTP at `https://api.anysearch.com/mcp` (anonymous or Bearer), and a Skill package already exists — the native tool plugin can be built and reviewed against a working endpoint rather than a spec.

**Questions for the maintainers** — we would rather ask before opening the PR:

1. **Category / overlap.** We could not find a published policy on category overlap (`CONTRIBUTING.md` is still `TODO`). Is another `search`-tagged provider welcome, or would you prefer it under a distinct tag or label to keep the category legible?
2. **Optional credentials.** Is an optional API key acceptable for a search-category provider, given that most existing providers require one? If not, we will make the key required and drop the anonymous path in the plugin.
3. **Risk classification.** `POST /v1/extract` fetches user-supplied URLs. Reading `docs/plugin-submission-requirements.md`, we believe that places the plugin at High risk ("proxy or crawl arbitrary URLs"). We intend to declare High and constrain inputs, set request timeouts, and avoid leaking credentials in errors. Please confirm that is the level you expect, and whether a High-risk plugin in the search category is acceptable.
4. **Exposed tag set.** The live catalog is broader than what a typical Dify user needs, and includes health, financial and legal data alongside some legally sensitive sources. We are happy to restrict the tag set the plugin exposes. Would you like us to, and do you have guidance on which verticals a search provider in the Marketplace should surface?
5. **Listing path.** We assume the expected route is a PR to `langgenius/dify-plugins` adding `anysearch/anysearch/anysearch-<version>.difypkg`, with `PRIVACY.md`, a source-repository link and an English README. If you would instead prefer to handle AnySearch as an official / featured integration, or an MCP-only listing, tell us and we will follow that path.

We are happy to adjust scope to whatever keeps the Marketplace coherent. Thanks.

### Official Website URL

https://anysearch.com/docs

issues.title: Kubernetes sandbox backend (no Docker socket)
issues.body:
## Problem

Every sandbox starts a sibling container through the `docker` CLI and
`/var/run/docker.sock`. That covers Agent Python tools and skills, the Code
node and its formatter, custom Playwright, MCP stdio, and the Codex and
OpenCode wrappers.

Some Kubernetes nodes have no Docker daemon: Talos, Bottlerocket,
containerd-only pools on EKS, AKS and GKE, and OpenShift. There, the only
choice is `HEYM_*_SANDBOX=subprocess`, which the docs call trusted
single-user only, or nothing. The Code node, Codex and OpenCode have no
fallback and fail.

## Who hits it

Anyone self-hosting Heym on Kubernetes, where mounting the host's Docker
socket is either impossible or not something you would want to do.

## Proposed approach

Three PRs, each releasable on its own:

1. **No behaviour change.** Move the nine `docker run` builders behind one
   `SandboxSpec` plus a `DockerRunner`. Parity tests assert that the argv
   stays the same, flag for flag. This also removes the five copies of
   `_docker_available`, `_resolve_image` and `_force_remove_container`.
2. **`HEYM_SANDBOX_BACKEND=kubernetes`, for the stdin/stdout-only sites:**
   the Python tool, the Code formatter, the Code node without requirements,
   and Playwright.
    - Each run is one Pod in a configurable namespace, under Pod Security
      `restricted`, with no ServiceAccount token.
    - `--network none|bridge` becomes a pod label that operator-provided
      NetworkPolicies select.
    - It is built on `httpx` and `websockets`, so there is no new dependency.
    - It fails closed exactly as the Docker path does.
3. **Workspaces.** Skills, Code node requirements and MCP stdio first, then
   Codex and OpenCode. There are two modes, and each run sees only its own
   files in both:
    - `stream` (default): a tar over the pod's attach stream, the same way
      `kubectl cp` moves files. No storage needed.
    - `volume`: an RWX PVC mounted with `subPath` set to the run's directory,
      the Kubernetes equivalent of today's `volume-subpath`.

Docker stays the default. No schema, migration, UI or public API changes.

## Touches

- `backend/app/services/*_executor.py`
- `mcp_stdio_sandbox.py`
- `playwright_sandbox.py`
- `code_formatter.py`
- `docker/heym-*-docker`
- `ENVIRONMENT-VARIABLES.md`

## Questions

1. Do you want a Kubernetes backend in-tree, or would you rather Docker stay
   the only supported sandbox?
2. Is the `SandboxSpec` plus runner shape right for PR 1? I'd rather agree on
   it here than in a large diff.
3. Codex's bubblewrap cannot run in a `restricted` pod. Is
   `--sandbox danger-full-access` acceptable when the pod is the boundary?
4. Would a Helm chart help, either in-tree under `deploy/helm/` or as a
   separate community chart on Artifact Hub? It would package Heym plus the
   sandbox namespace, RBAC and NetworkPolicies, with presets for OpenShift,
   EKS, AKS and GKE. I'd maintain it, including tag bumps.

I have a prototype that matches the current argv of all nine call sites and
am happy to share it. I'll wait for your go-ahead on scope, and can talk it
through on Discord first if that's easier.

issues.title: Flagship eval did not pass on v0.25.4-rc1
issues.body:
The flagship eval on release tag `v0.25.4-rc1` did not pass. Publishing is not blocked by it.

- Run: https://github.com/amd/gaia/actions/runs/41148504198
- Tier: `smoke` (eval/ci_tiers.json)
- Scenario lanes: `failure`
- Outcomes (`gaia eval tasks`): `skipped`
- Final tag, full sweep found for this commit or an RC: `skipped` (`skipped` on an RC)

Start with the run's summary page: it names which lanes measured, which measured nothing, and
how long each took. Then download the failing lane's `eval-<lane>` artifact - it carries the
transcripts, judge rationales, backend log and Lemonade logs. Those machines are ephemeral and
already destroyed, so the artifact is the only copy, and it expires in 14 days.

Compare with the previous tag's run first. A failure no change since then explains usually means
the environment moved, not the code: a Lemonade version bump, a re-quantised model, a driver or
runner-image change.

`cancelled` rather than `failure` means no measurement happened at all - a manual cancel, or a
lane that waited out GitHub's 24h queue limit. Re-dispatch the workflow on the tag.

A passing re-run closes this issue, and so does a later passing tag on the same major.minor line
whose tier covers this one (a full sweep covers smoke). A final tag's issue closes only on its own
passing re-run.

issues.title: ImportError: DLL load failed while importing _cache: Access is denied on Windows starting in v0.149.16 (Regression from v0.149.12)
issues.body:
Description:
Environment
OS: Windows 10/11

Python Version: 3.12.12

Package Manager: uv (v0.149.16 fails, v0.149.12 works)

Describe the bug
When upgrading zeroconf to version 0.149.16 on Windows, importing the library fails with an ImportError: DLL load failed while importing _cache: Access is denied. error. Downgrading the package back to 0.149.12 completely resolves the issue, indicating a potential regression introduced in the built C-extensions (_cache.pyd) in the latest release wheel.

Steps to Reproduce
Create/use a Python 3.12 environment on Windows.

Force reinstall version 0.149.16.

Try to import the library via terminal.

uv pip install --force-reinstall "zeroconf==0.149.16"
python -c "import zeroconf"
